title: Feedback-driven probe rebalancer for cohort-aware canary stability
author: Maya Liu
description: Context: Production canary evaluations have become noisy for heterogeneous traffic shapes resulting in false positives and wasted rollout budget. Motivation: static probe allocation ignores cohort-level drift and can miss regressions that only affect a subset of traffic. Proposal: implement a Feedback-Driven Probe Rebalancer (FDPR) that continuously reweights synthetic probe allocation across traffic cohorts based on short-term SLI signals (p50/p95/p99 latency deltas, error rates, throughput divergence). FDPR combines an EWMA signal smoother with a conservative reweighting step and an exploration floor (small randomized probe fraction) to surface latent regressions. The controller emits per-cohort allocation decisions to the probe scheduler and exposes metrics for audit/alerting. This PR contains controller, scheduler integration, metrics aggregation, new dashboards, e2e traffic harness and rollout guard wiring. Design highlights: 1) Stability-first reweighting: min_delta thresholds and hysteresis to avoid oscillation; 2) Signal fusion: latency+error+throughput fusion with tunable weights; 3) Safety gate: rebalancing is constrained by a max_shift_per_minute parameter and disabled automatically under high traffic variance; 4) Feature flagged opt-in and a staged rollout plan behind existing canary rollout guards. Testing: unit tests for rebalancer logic, integration tests with synthetic traffic generator, stress test in benchmark-lab, and staging canary run with shadowed production traffic. Rollout plan: merge disabled by default; enable in staging for 48h; pilot on two customer-facing clusters with close SRE monitoring; promote to GA after 2 weeks of stable signal. Backward compatibility: none of the core probe APIs changed; default behaviour unchanged when disabled. Related items: design doc https://linear.app/redwood/issue/ENG-4821/fdpr-design and follow-up analysis ENG-4988. Checklist: [x] design doc linked; [x] unit/integration tests; [x] dashboards and alerts; [x] rollout playbook; [x] docs update.

review_comments: Ethan Kim: Nice approach, two quick asks: (1) please add a guard when the number of cohorts drops below the min_cohort threshold to prevent division by zero; (2) can you make the max_shift_per_minute configurable by cluster?
Maya Liu: Thanks Ethan, added min_cohort guard and cluster-level override for max_shift_per_minute in the latest commit.
Priya Shah: Please add a note in docs about interaction with traffic-weighted canary and clarify defaults for exploration floor.
Maya Liu: Expanded docs and added default values section; left exploration floor at 2% as conservative starting point.
Lina Ortega: CI flaked on integration test first run; reran and it passed. Approving after one small nit on log message severity.
Maya Liu: Adjusted log verbosity to debug for frequent rebalancer ticks per Lina's suggestion.
Ethan Kim: Approving - observed stable behaviour in staging run, metrics look good.
release_notes: Adds Feedback-Driven Probe Rebalancer to dynamically allocate canary probes across traffic cohorts; feature-gated and disabled by default; includes metrics, dashboards, and a staged rollout plan. Config knobs: perf.rebalancer.max_shift_per_minute, perf.rebalancer.exploration_floor, perf.rebalancer.enabled.
